text:
The Grand Chamber held on 21 November 2001 that the United Kingdom did not violate the Convention by applying Kuwait’s state immunity and striking out Al-Adsani’s civil damages claim for alleged torture. It found no violation of Article 3 unanimously, and no violation of Article 6 § 1 by nine votes to eight, because the immunity bar pursued a legitimate aim and, as a generally recognised rule of international law, was a proportionate limit on access to a court in civil proceedings. The Court did not hold that sovereign immunity overrides every competing Convention guarantee; it confined the ruling to that civil claim and was not persuaded that the jus cogens status of the torture prohibition had yet created a civil-proceedings exception to immunity.

CONFIDENCE: 90
